n4.hw.ueberlast: The administration is handling {n} projects at once: implementation takes {prozent}% longer.
n4.hw.luecke: You are expected to be {n} votes short. You can win them in parliament from individual deputies, in return for a pledge, a post or a favour.
n4.hw.kleinerOrt: A small area: little effect on national figures, but clearly felt locally.
n4.hw.umfang: {prozent}% of the population is affected. The political price is {preis}% of the nationwide price; budget costs follow population ({bip}% of GDP a year).
n4.hw.umfangKlein: Less than 1% of the population is affected. The political price is {preis}% of the nationwide price; budget costs follow population ({bip}% of GDP a year).
n4.hw.ruecknahme: Reversing is dearer: {f} times the capital of introducing it, because those who benefit fight back.
n4.hw.dauerlast: Ongoing burden: about {n} capital a month at full level, pro rata to the current level.
n4.weg.grund.gesetz: Only a law can settle this. A presidential decree is not permitted here (Constitution Art. 104(17)).
n4.weg.grund.haushalt: This is budget money: higher spending needs a law and the budget, not a decree (Constitution Art. 161).
n4.weg.grund.kommission: The minimum wage is set by the Minimum Wage Commission (Labour Act Art. 39). You instruct your five government representatives on it.
n4.weg.grund.notstand: Emergency decrees and a state of emergency exist only once you declare a state of emergency (Constitution Art. 119).
n4.grund.nichtMoeglich: That is not possible right now.
n4.grund.ende: The term of office has ended.
n4.grund.wegeStattVerbote: The route via a law remains open.
n4.grund.kapitalErlass: Not enough capital for the decree: {n} needed, {da} available.
n4.grund.kapitalBeschluss: Not enough capital for the presidential decision: {n} needed, {da} available.
n4.grund.kapitalWarum: Capital grows with trust and a majority; not everything at once.
n4.grund.schonImParlament: There is already a bill on “{name}” before parliament.
n4.grund.nichtMehrDa: This bill is no longer pending.
n4.log.gesetztWarum: {text} Implementation takes about {monate, plural, one {one month} other {# months}}.
n4.log.gesetztKostet: {text} Implementation takes about {monate, plural, one {one month} other {# months}}; costs about {bip}% of GDP a year.
n4.log.gesetztBringt: {text} Implementation takes about {monate, plural, one {one month} other {# months}}; raises about {bip}% of GDP a year.
n4.beschluss.text: Presidential decision: {name} from “{von}” to “{nach}”, within the limits set by law.
n4.beschluss.warum: Costs {pk} capital. A decision takes effect at once, without a vote; it holds only within what the law permits (Constitution Art. 73).
n4.erlass.warum: {why} A decree bypasses parliament and costs {pk} capital and some trust.
n4.gesetz.eingebracht: At your request your parliamentary group introduces “{name}” {ort}: new level “{ziel}”. The committee first deliberates for {ausschuss} days, the vote is on {datum}; implementation then takes about {monate, plural, one {one month} other {# months}}.
n4.gesetz.eingebrachtWarum: {pk} capital paid. {ja} supporters are expected (range {tief} to {hoch}); with normal attendance {noetig} are enough for a majority of those present (Constitution Art. 96).
n4.gesetz.verzug: Introduction is delayed by two days: under strain you lack focus.
n4.gesetz.neinWarum: The capital committed ({pk}) is lost and the government looks weakened. Of {anwesend} members present, no majority voted in favour; withdrawing beforehand would have saved {gerettet} capital.
n4.rueckzug.warum: {zurueck} of {pk} capital is returned. Withdrawing is cheaper than losing a vote.
n4.kommission.einberufen: The Labour Ministry convenes the Minimum Wage Commission. Your instruction to the five government representatives: “{ziel}”. Decision on {datum}.
n4.kommission.warum: Costs {pk} capital. The commission has fifteen members: five from the state, five from workers, five from employers. With either side the state prevails; the decision is final.
n4.kommission.erhoeht: The Minimum Wage Commission decides 10 to 5: {name} from “{von}” to “{nach}”. The employers vote against.
n4.kommission.erhoehtWarum: The state and the workers' representatives form the majority. The decision is published in the Resmî Gazete and applies at once.
n4.kommission.gesenkt: The Minimum Wage Commission decides 10 to 5: {name} from “{von}” to “{nach}”. The workers' representatives vote against.
n4.kommission.gesenktWarum: The state and the employers form the majority. The decision is published in the Resmî Gazete and applies at once.
n4.ausschuss.keinSchritt: This bill cannot be softened any further.
n4.ausschuss.kompromissText: Committee compromise: your group softens “{name}”, now “{ziel}”.
n4.ausschuss.kompromissWarum: A smaller step wins votes: {vorher} expected before, {ja} now.
n4.ausschuss.geaendert: The committee amends “{name}”: the draft now says “{ziel}” instead of “{vorher}”. Your camp has no majority there.
n4.ausschuss.geaendertWarum: Committee seats follow the strength of the groups. If the plenary adopts the amended text, you may sign it or send it back within 15 days (Constitution Art. 89).
n4.unterschrift.vorlage: Parliament adopts “{name}” ({ja} to {nein}). The law awaits your signature: {tage} days to promulgate or return it.
n4.unterschrift.vorlageWarum: The committee changed the draft. If you neither sign nor return it, it is deemed promulgated when the period ends (Constitution Art. 89).
n4.rueckgabe.text: You return “{name}” to parliament with your reasons. It will reconsider in {tage} days; unchanged, the law stands only with {noetig} yes votes of the members.
n4.rueckgabe.warum: The opposition calls it a veto against parliament; a little trust is lost. Budget laws cannot be returned (Constitution Art. 89).
n4.rueckgabe.ueberstimmt: Parliament re-adopts “{name}” unchanged: {ja} yes, {noetig} were needed. You must promulgate it.
n4.rueckgabe.ueberstimmtWarum: With an absolute majority of its members, parliament prevails over the president (Constitution Art. 89).
n4.rueckgabe.gescheitert: After your return, “{name}” gets only {ja} yes votes; {noetig} would be needed. The law is not promulgated.
n4.rueckgabe.gescheitertWarum: Without a majority of members the law lapses. You can have your own version introduced again later.
n4.abs.veraltet: This offer no longer stands. The situation has changed.
n4.abs.keine: There is nobody left to win over right now.
n4.abs.zusageText: {wer} ({partei}, {provinz}) and {n} other deputies vote for “{name}”; in return the government meets their demand: {forderung}.
n4.abs.posten.text: {wer} ({partei}, {provinz}) brings {n} votes for “{name}”. In return a member of the group gets a post.
n4.abs.gefallen.text: {wer} ({partei}, {provinz}) brings {n} votes for “{name}”. In return the government does the province a favour.
n4.abs.warum: Costs {pk} capital. Risk of press exposure: {risiko}.
n4.abs.zusage.aufgedeckt: The press reveals: {wer} and {n} {partei} deputies voted for “{name}” in return for a government pledge.
n4.abs.posten.aufgedeckt: The press reveals: a post for the group around {wer} ({partei}) secured {n} votes for “{name}”.
n4.abs.gefallen.aufgedeckt: The press reveals: a favour for {provinz} brought {n} {partei} votes for “{name}”.
n4.abs.aufgedecktWarum: Vote-buying damages trust in the government and costs approval.
n4.not.keinAnlass: There are no grounds under Art. 119: no war, no disaster, no serious unrest, no terrorism and no severe economic crisis.
n4.not.schonAktiv: The state of emergency is already in force, until {datum}.
n4.not.nichtAktiv: No state of emergency is in force.
n4.not.ausgerufen: State of emergency declared (grounds: {anlass}). Parliament confirms the same day, {ja} to {nein}. It runs until {datum}.
n4.not.ausgerufenWarum: Costs {pk} capital and some trust. At most {tage} days; only parliament can extend it, by up to four months at a time (Constitution Art. 119).
n4.not.abgelehnt: Parliament rejects the state of emergency ({ja} to {nein}). It ends at once (grounds: {anlass}).
n4.not.abgelehntWarum: The capital committed ({pk}) is lost. No state of emergency holds without a majority in parliament.
n4.not.verlaengert: Parliament extends the state of emergency by {tage} days ({ja} to {nein}). It now runs until {datum}.
n4.not.verlaengertWarum: Costs {pk} capital and some trust. Each extension is a new vote.
n4.not.verlaengerungAbgelehnt: Parliament rejects the extension ({ja} to {nein}). The state of emergency ends on {datum}.
n4.not.verlaengerungAbgelehntWarum: The capital spent on the request is lost.
n4.not.aufgehoben: You lift the state of emergency after {tage} days.
n4.not.abgelaufen: The state of emergency expires after {tage} days.
n4.not.endeWarum: The special powers lapse; the level from before the declaration applies again.
n4.hr.z.wackelig: might vote yes from the opposition
